resale_co.name: Residential Certificate of Occupancy (Certificate of Inspection / Certificate of Continued Occupancy), Housing Code Chapter 155
resale_co.issued_by: Maple Shade Township Housing Inspection (Land Use / Community Development; Housing Inspector or Code Enforcement Officer)
resale_co.contact_title: Director of Community Development (Zoning Officer / Planning Administration)
resale_co.lead_time: No lead time published. Violations found at the first inspection must be fixed and re-inspected within 90 days (extendable once to 120 days if asked before day 90), or a new application and fee are needed.
resale_co.valid_for: Valid until the next sale, transfer or change of occupancy; not transferable to a new owner except between spouses or family members.
requirements: House numbers visible from the street, 4 inches high, contrasting color
Sidewalks, driveways and curbs without raised cracks over 1/2 inch or damage
Roof sound; signs of leaks need a licensed roofer's certification
Gutters and downspouts draining away from the building; front and rear exterior lights
Handrail on front steps with more than 3 risers; guardrails on decks and porches over 30 inches with balusters under 4 inches apart
Peeling paint scraped and painted; rotted wood, loose siding and broken glass repaired; screens on all windows
Yard cut and cleared; trash and recycling cans stored out of view from the street
10-year sealed battery smoke detector on every level and in every bedroom, none more than 10 years old; CO detectors within 10 feet of all sleeping areas
2A:10B:C fire extinguisher mounted in the kitchen area per NJ fire code
Graspable handrails on all stairs including basement; guards on open sides
Outlets, switches and fixtures working with covers; GFCI at kitchen counters, within 6 feet of sinks, bathrooms and washer
Windows open, close, lock and stay up; exterior door locks not keyed from inside; no infestation
Fireplaces and chimneys certified by a licensed contractor; termite damage needs an exterminator's certificate

Basement: water heater relief pipe within 6 inches of floor, emergency heater switch, sump pump to the outside (not the sewer), 60 amp minimum service with labeled breakers, hard-piped dryer vent, abandoned oil tanks removed with a permit
Stove anti-tip device; bedrooms need proper egress, and no basement bedrooms without egress; work done without permits must be permitted

fees.quote: The said fee for a Certificate of Transfer of Property Title is $75.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Residential Certificate of Occupancy (property, block and lot, seller, buyer, agent, rooms per floor, access contact), signed by owner and buyer, and submit it with the $125.00 fee by cash or check to Maple Shade Township Housing Inspection, 200 Stiles Avenue, Maple Shade, NJ 08052 (fax 856-779-2524, email Zoning@MapleShade.com). For an as-is sale where the buyer will not move in until repairs are done, use the Transfer of Title application instead ($75, one battery smoke detector per level); the buyer must then apply for the full CO within 120 days.

The following list is a general requirement checklist to prepare for a Maple Shade Township Housing Inspection prior to occupying any residential building.

resale_co.notes: The public notice on the CO page calls the new Housing Code 'Ordinance No. 2025-14', but the ordinance file posted by the Township is Ordinance 2025-18 (Chapter 155 'Housing Code'), introduced October 16, 2025 and adopted November 20, 2025, effective on adoption and publication. Its $125 and $65 fees match the $125.00 on the Residential CO Form (file posted January 2026). The checklist (posted March 2026) says each property may also be cited for violations not on the list. The Director of Community Development's email shows on the Township site as zoning@mapleshade.com (decoded from the site's email protection); the same address is printed on the form. Code Enforcement Officer Michael Anyzek, ext. 171, part-time. Commercial properties have a separate fee schedule in the ordinance.

requirements: Smoke detectors: 10-year sealed battery units, one on each level and one in each bedroom; no detector more than 10 years old (Township checklist, March 2026)
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of all sleeping areas
Fire extinguisher still listed on the March 2026 Township checklist: 2A:10B:C, mounted per NJ fire code in the kitchen area
For an as-is Transfer of Title sale (no one moving in): at least one battery smoke detector on each level, inspected before the transfer certificate is issued

fire_cert.notes: The DCA registry lists Maple Shade as a municipal fire code enforcing agency (code M). The DCA directory lists 'Maple Shade Fire Prev', 200 Stiles Ave, (856) 779-1335 as the Smoke Detector Compliance contact and Fire Official Matthew Orsini at (856) 779-9610, firemarshal@mapleshade.com. The Township's Fire Official page now says the Resale Smoke Alarm Application was replaced by the Residential CO Form, so the smoke and CO check for a sale runs through the Housing CO inspection. Fire Prevention Specialist Shelby Holzinger, ext. 183 (sholzinger@mapleshade.com), is also listed. The March 2026 checklist still lists a 2A:10B:C fire extinguisher even though P.L.2025, c.19 dropped it from the state rule. The checklist asks for 10-year sealed battery detectors; it does not say how homes with hard-wired alarms are handled.

other_items.label: Work done without permits
other_items.detail: Permits are needed for new wiring, plumbing, electrical service or panel, heater, A/C, water heater and similar work. A buyer of a home with unpermitted improvements takes on getting and closing those permits.

other_items.label: As-is (rehab / fixer upper) sales
other_items.detail: The home must stay vacant until permits and CO approvals are done. A Certificate for Transfer of Property Title ($75, valid 120 days) allows the closing; the full CO application must be filed before it expires.
